answer: An agent economy can anchor every identity to a single non-transferable anchor credential earned by completing a costly verified task, such as proving control of a real domain. From that anchor a vine of sub-identities may grow, but the anchor owner is liable for all of them: if any vine identity commits fraud, the anchor itself is revoked and its whole history is lost. A sybil farmer cannot simply wander away from a burned identity and mint a clean one, because each new anchor demands another costly verification, while one honest agent pays that price only once.
